questions.stem: The order of events in a four-stroke engine is:
options: Power, intake, compression, exhaust
Intake, compression, power, exhaust
Exhaust, power, intake, compression
Compression, intake, exhaust, power
questions.explanation: Memorise the cycle: suck, squeeze, bang, blow.

questions.stem: A diesel engine ignites its fuel by:
options: A spark plug
A pilot flame
Heat of compression
A glow pipe in every cylinder
questions.explanation: Air compressed hot enough ignites injected fuel.

options: The number of valves per cylinder
The clearance in the valve train
The strength of the valve springs
The wear limit of the valve seat
questions.explanation: Correct lash ensures valves open and close properly.

options: Diesel engines with high-pressure fuel injection pumps
Gasoline engines, where it mixes air and fuel
Electric propulsion motors and generators
Steam turbines, where it meters the steam
questions.explanation: Diesel engines inject fuel directly, with no carburettor.

options: Cools the fuel before it reaches the injectors
Filters sea water out of the fuel supply
Delivers metered high-pressure fuel at the right time
Starts the engine electrically from the battery
questions.explanation: Timing and quantity control engine power and efficiency.

questions.stem: A spark plug ignition system is used on:
options: Air compressors
Hydraulic rams
Gasoline engines
Diesel engines in cold weather
questions.explanation: Diesel engines rely on heat of compression.

questions.stem: In a two-stroke engine, scavenging means:
options: Blowing fresh air through to push out the burnt gas
Cleaning carbon off the fuel injector nozzles
Draining used oil from the crankcase sump
Cooling the pistons with a spray of sea water
questions.explanation: Scavenging clears the exhaust and refills the cylinder with fresh air, usually with a blower or pump.

questions.stem: A turbocharger increases engine power by:
options: Cooling the exhaust so the engine runs cooler
Adding more fuel from extra tanks under pressure
Increasing the stroke of the pistons at high engine speed
Using exhaust gas to drive a compressor for more air
questions.explanation: More air lets more fuel be burned, so the engine makes more power.

questions.stem: The scraper (oil control) ring on a piston:
options: Seals combustion gas above the piston crown
Holds the piston pin in place in the boss
Wipes surplus oil off the liner back to the sump
Cools the exhaust valve by carrying oil up to its stem
questions.explanation: The compression rings seal gas. The scraper ring controls oil so it does not burn.

questions.stem: In a diesel engine, the speed is kept steady as load changes by the:
options: Throttle valve, which limits the air
Thermostat, which holds the coolant temperature
Governor, which adjusts the fuel delivered
Turbocharger, which matches air to load
questions.explanation: A diesel has no air throttle. Output is controlled by how much fuel is injected.
